# T6.02: the HEVC structures in nvenc_drv.h

Read the H.265 part of `vendor/open-gpu-doc/classes/video/nvenc_drv.h` and compared it with the H.264 structures
`src/enc.c` fills. Sizes checked by compiling the header (clang, x86_64): every size matches the header's comments.

## Picture setup: `nvenc_h265_drv_pic_setup_s`, 1024 bytes (H.264: 512)

| offset | field | size | vs H.264 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `magic` | 4 | same |
| 4 / 36 / 68 | `refpic_cfg`, `input_cfg`, `outputpic_cfg` (`nvenc_h265_surface_cfg_s`) | 32 each | same layout as `nvenc_h264_surface_cfg_s` (size, pitch, offsets in 256 B units, `block_height`, `tiled_16x16`, `memory_mode`, `input_bl_mode`) |
| 100 | `sps_data` | 8 | new content: chroma format, `log2_max_pic_order_cnt_lsb_minus4`, min/max CU and TU size, transform depths, AMP, strong intra smoothing, SAO, temporal MVP, number of short-term RPS, bit depth |
| 108 | `pps_data` | 8 | new content: `num_ref_idx_l0_active_minus1`, `cu_qp_delta_enabled_flag`, `diff_cu_qp_delta_depth`, `sign_data_hiding`, `transform_skip`, deblocking override, `pic_init_qp_minus26`, `log2_parallel_merge_level_minus2`, ... |
| 116 | `rate_control` (`nvenc_h265_rc_s`) | 96 | the H.264 RC (88 B) plus `ext_*` hints and `session_max_qp`; QP/minQP/maxQP, `Ravg`, `R`, `framerate`, `gop_length`, `single_frame_vbv`, `i_size_ratio` as in M3 |
| 212 | `pic_control` (`nvenc_h265_pic_control_s`) | 536 | see below |
| 748 | `half_scaled_outputpic_cfg` | 32 | same |
| 780 | `gpTimer_timeout_val` | 4 | same |
| 784 | reserved | 240 | pad to 1024 |

`pic_control`, the per-picture part. Same as H.264: `l0`/`l1`, `temp_dist_l0`, `dist_scale_factor`, the
`num_*_controls_minus1` counts and `*_control_offset`s (relative to the start of the setup), `hist_buf_size`,
`bitstream_buf_size`, `bitstream_start_pos`, `pic_type` (0 P, 1 B, 2 I, 3 IDR), `ref_pic_flag`, `slice_mode`.
New for HEVC:
- `codec` (3 bits), `ceil_log2_pic_size_in_ctbs` (6 bits: the driver computes ceil(log2(number of CTBs)) for the HW),
  `sao_luma_mode` / `sao_chroma_mode`.
- `pic_order_cnt_lsb`, `nal_unit_type`, `nuh_temporal_id_plus1`, `e4byteStartCode`, `no_output_of_prior_pics_flag`,
  `pic_output_flag`.
- Reference sets: `short_term_ref_pic_set_sps_flag` / `_idx`, an inline `short_term_rps` (`nvenc_h265_strps_s`, 80 B:
  `num_negative_pics`, `delta_poc_s0_minus1[]`, `used_by_curr_pic_s0_flag`, ...), `long_term_rps` (120 B),
  `ref_pic_list_modification` (36 B), `poc_entry_l0/l1`, `same_poc`, `longTermFlag`.
- `enable_source_image_padding` + luma/chroma padding modes (HW pads the source to the CTB grid).
- `cu_early_terminatiom_enable`, `slice_encoding_row_start/num`, strips, MV-HEVC fields (unused for us).

## Controls appended after the setup (offsets in `pic_control`)

| control | struct | size | vs H.264 |
|---|---|---|---|
| motion estimation | `nvenc_h264_me_control_s` | 192 | **the H.264 struct is reused** (no H.265 ME struct; the comments in `pic_control` name the H.264 types) |
| mode decision | `nvenc_h265_md_control_s` | 128 | new: intra mode masks per block size (4x4 to 64x64), CU partition enables per CU size (16/32/64), intra/TU size enables, `pskip_enable`, biases per PU/CU size |
| quantization | `nvenc_h265_quant_control_s` | 16 | new (H.264: `nvenc_h264_quant_control_s`) |
| slices | `nvenc_h265_slice_control_s` | 64 | new |

## Methods

The class (`clc9b7.h`) has no HEVC-only methods. HEVC uses the methods `enc.c` already sends:
`SET_APPLICATION_ID` with `NVC9B7_SET_APPLICATION_ID_ID_NVENC_H265` (3), `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS`, `SET_IN_DRV_PIC_SETUP`,
`SET_IN_CUR_PIC(_CHROMA)`, `SET_IN/OUT_REF_PIC_*`, `SET_OUT_BITSTREAM`, `SET_OUT_ENC_STATUS`, `SET_IOHISTORY`,
`SET_IN/OUT_COLOC_DATA`, `SET_IN/OUT_MEPRED_DATA`, `SET_IN_RCDATA`, `SET_IO_RC_PROCESS`.

## Not in the documentation (for T6.03, observing nullmoth's `libnvenc_hevc`)

1. `SET_CONTROL_PARAMS_CODEC_TYPE`: only H.264 (3) is defined.
2. `pic_control.codec`: values not given.
3. CTB size the HW expects (`max_cu_size` 32 or 64), min CU/TU, transform depths, and the matching
   `ceil_log2_pic_size_in_ctbs`.
4. Which ME/MD/quant values make a valid HEVC picture (for H.264 the engine hung on some combinations: `slice_mode`
   and the intra SSD counts, M2 notes).
5. Buffer sizes for HEVC: history, colocated data, MEPRED, and whether recon planes keep the 32-row rounding from M2.
6. Whether the input surface uses the same measured 64x16 tile layout as H.264 (M2).
7. Slice header contents the engine writes vs what the driver expects us to have put in VPS/SPS/PPS (`nal_unit_type`
   for IDR: 19 IDR_W_RADL or 20 IDR_N_LP).
